drills.title: Revenue by segment
drills.prompt: Return each customer segment and paid revenue, highest revenue first.
drills.brief: Interview SQL is mostly grain control: decide what one row means before joining.
drills.example: Aggregate orders only after joining each order to its single customer.
drills.starter_answer:
SELECT
  -- segment and paid revenue
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
drills.expected_sql: SELECT c.segment, ROUND(SUM(o.revenue), 2) FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE o.status='paid' GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY SUM(o.revenue) DESC

hints.conceptual: Filter to paid orders and group at segment grain.
hints.pattern: JOIN customers to orders, WHERE status, GROUP BY segment.

drills.solution: SELECT c.segment, ROUND(SUM(o.revenue), 2) AS paid_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE o.status='paid' GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY paid_revenue DESC;
drills.debrief: The filter belongs before aggregation; the customer join supplies the segment.

drills.title: Delinquency by FICO band
drills.prompt: Return each FICO band with its loan count and delinquent-loan count, ordered by FICO band.
drills.brief: Transfer means preserving the same grain reasoning on unfamiliar tables.
drills.example: Use conditional aggregation when a denominator and subset share one group.
drills.starter_answer:
SELECT
FROM borrowers b
JOIN loans l ON l.borrower_id = b.borrower_id
drills.expected_sql: SELECT b.fico_band, COUNT(*), SUM(CASE WHEN l.status='delinquent' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM borrowers b JOIN loans l ON l.borrower_id=b.borrower_id GROUP BY b.fico_band ORDER BY b.fico_band

hints.conceptual: Count all joined loans, then conditionally count delinquent ones.
hints.pattern: SUM(CASE WHEN condition THEN 1 ELSE 0 END).

drills.solution: SELECT b.fico_band, COUNT(*) AS loans, SUM(CASE WHEN l.status='delinquent' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS delinquent FROM borrowers b JOIN loans l ON l.borrower_id=b.borrower_id GROUP BY b.fico_band ORDER BY b.fico_band;
drills.debrief: Both measures use loan grain, so one grouped query is sufficient.

drills.title: Design a trustworthy A/B test
drills.prompt: Design a test for a faster checkout. State the unit, primary metric, guardrails, and two validity risks.
drills.brief: A good experiment answer starts with a decision, not a statistical test name.
drills.example: Randomize at the user level when repeat visits could contaminate sessions.

rubric.label: Randomization unit
rubric.description: Names a stable assignment unit and why.

rubric.label: Primary metric
rubric.description: Defines a decision-linked conversion metric with denominator.

rubric.label: Guardrails
rubric.description: Protects errors, latency, refunds, or revenue quality.

rubric.label: Validity risks
rubric.description: Identifies at least two risks such as novelty, sample ratio mismatch, peeking, or contamination.

hints.conceptual: Connect assignment, outcome, safety, and validity.
hints.pattern: Unit → primary metric → guardrails → risks.

drills.solution: Randomize persistent users, measure completed checkouts per eligible user, guard errors/refunds/revenue, pre-size the test, and monitor sample-ratio mismatch and novelty.
drills.debrief: The design is credible when every metric has a population and every threat has a mitigation.

drills.title: Evaluate a lending policy
drills.prompt: A new underwriting rule lowers approvals. Explain how you would estimate its effect on delinquency without harming applicants.
drills.brief: Some policies cannot be randomized naively; explain identification and ethics.
drills.example: A staged rollout can create comparison groups while limiting exposure.

rubric.label: Identification
rubric.description: Proposes a staged, threshold, matched, or shadow-mode comparison.

rubric.label: Outcomes
rubric.description: Balances approval/access and repayment outcomes.

rubric.label: Fairness
rubric.description: Checks subgroup impact and avoids protected-feature misuse.

hints.conceptual: Balance causal identification with applicant safety and fairness.
hints.pattern: Design → outcomes → confounding → subgroup checks.

drills.solution: Use shadow mode or a staged rollout, compare repayment and approval outcomes, adjust for threshold selection, and pre-specify subgroup fairness checks.
drills.debrief: A lower delinquency rate is not automatically better if access falls or the comparison is selected.

drills.title: Build a KPI tree
drills.prompt: Define a north-star and input/guardrail metrics for a two-sided services marketplace.
drills.brief: A metric is useful only when its movement changes a decision.
drills.example: Completed matches can be decomposed into active demand, fill rate, and completion rate.

rubric.label: North star
rubric.description: Names fulfilled value, not raw activity.

rubric.label: Inputs
rubric.description: Decomposes demand, supply, conversion, and repeat behavior.

rubric.label: Guardrails
rubric.description: Protects quality, cancellation, latency, or economics.

hints.conceptual: Measure delivered customer value, its drivers, and ways it can be gamed.
hints.pattern: North star = demand × match × completion; add quality/economic guardrails.

drills.solution: Use completed high-quality services as the north star, decompose active demand, supply coverage, match and completion rates, and guard cancellation, quality, time-to-match, and contribution margin.
drills.debrief: The tree is strongest when each child explains a change in its parent.

drills.title: Protect revenue quality
drills.prompt: Sales proposes gross bookings as the only KPI. Build a better revenue scorecard and explain denominator risks.
drills.brief: Revenue metrics need quality, timing, and denominator discipline.
drills.example: Bookings can rise while refunds and acquisition cost destroy contribution.

rubric.label: Revenue definition
rubric.description: Distinguishes bookings, recognized revenue, and cash.

rubric.label: Quality
rubric.description: Includes margin, refunds, retention, or bad debt.

rubric.label: Denominator
rubric.description: Defines cohort, active account, or time basis consistently.

hints.conceptual: Separate volume from durable economic value.
hints.pattern: Bookings → recognized revenue → gross/contribution margin; guard refunds and retention.

drills.solution: Track bookings, recognized revenue, contribution margin, refunds, bad debt, and cohort retention using consistent active-customer and calendar denominators.
drills.debrief: A scorecard prevents teams from winning the volume metric while losing economics.

drills.title: Diagnose a funnel drop
drills.prompt: Checkout completion fell 12% week over week while traffic rose. Give an investigation sequence and a cautious recommendation.
drills.brief: Interpretation is a chain: verify, segment, explain, decide.
drills.example: First distinguish a real behavior change from instrumentation or denominator changes.

rubric.label: Verify
rubric.description: Checks instrumentation, denominator, freshness, and release timing.

rubric.label: Segment
rubric.description: Segments by device, channel, market, or step.

rubric.label: Action
rubric.description: Ties action strength to evidence and reversibility.

hints.conceptual: Validate the signal before explaining it.
hints.pattern: Quality check → locate segment/step → form hypotheses → reversible action.

drills.solution: Check tracking and denominators, localize by platform/channel/funnel step and release, then roll back only if the drop aligns with a change; otherwise investigate with a bounded test.
drills.debrief: A chart does not identify cause; the investigation narrows what evidence would.

drills.title: Explain a retention illusion
drills.prompt: Overall retention rose, but every acquisition-channel cohort declined. Explain how this can happen and what to show next.
drills.brief: Aggregates can reverse subgroup trends when the mix changes.
drills.example: A larger share of historically high-retention users can lift the total.

rubric.label: Composition
rubric.description: Identifies mix shift or Simpson's paradox.

rubric.label: Next view
rubric.description: Requests weighted cohorts, standardized mix, or channel/time cuts.

rubric.label: Decision caution
rubric.description: Avoids claiming product improvement from aggregate movement.

hints.conceptual: Ask whether subgroup weights changed.
hints.pattern: Name Simpson's paradox, standardize the mix, compare like-for-like cohorts.

drills.solution: A shift toward a high-retention channel can raise the aggregate despite within-channel declines. Show channel cohorts and a mix-standardized overall rate before acting.
drills.debrief: The weighted average changed because both rates and weights moved.

drills.title: Group paid revenue
drills.prompt: Using the provided orders records, return paid revenue by customer_id as sorted records.
drills.brief: Pandas interviews test explicit filtering, grouping, and output shape.
drills.example: Filter first, then group and reset the index to make the grain visible.

hints.conceptual: Exclude non-paid rows before grouping.
hints.pattern: df.loc[mask].groupby(key, as_index=False)[value].sum().sort_values(key).

drills.solution: result = orders.loc[orders.status.eq('paid')].groupby('customer_id', as_index=False).revenue.sum().sort_values('customer_id')
drills.debrief: Filtering before aggregation keeps refunds and pending orders out of the metric.

drills.title: Flag late payments
drills.prompt: Return loan_id and late_days for paid records where paid_at is after due_at, sorted by loan_id.
drills.brief: Date arithmetic is where hidden null and type assumptions surface.
drills.example: Convert both columns explicitly before subtracting.

hints.conceptual: Parse dates, exclude unpaid rows, then subtract.
hints.pattern: (paid_at - due_at).dt.days followed by a positive-day filter.

drills.solution: payments[['due_at','paid_at']] = payments[['due_at','paid_at']].apply(pd.to_datetime); payments['late_days']=(payments.paid_at-payments.due_at).dt.days; result=payments.loc[payments.late_days.gt(0), ['loan_id','late_days']].sort_values('loan_id')
drills.debrief: Null paid dates remain NaT and naturally fail the positive-day condition.

drills.title: Model commerce analytics
drills.prompt: Design a star schema for order revenue, refunds, customers, products, and daily reporting. State every fact grain.
drills.brief: Data models fail when grain remains implicit.
drills.example: Order line and payment transaction are different facts and should not be forced into one row.

rubric.label: Fact grain
rubric.description: States order-line and refund/payment grains explicitly.

rubric.label: Dimensions
rubric.description: Defines customer, product, and date dimensions with keys.

rubric.label: History
rubric.description: Addresses changing attributes without rewriting facts.

hints.conceptual: Name the event represented by one fact row.
hints.pattern: Facts by business event; conformed customer/product/date dimensions; SCD choice.

drills.solution: Use order_line and payment/refund facts at their native event grains, conformed customer/product/date dimensions, and Type 2 customer attributes only where historical reporting requires them.
drills.debrief: Separate facts avoid fan-out and preserve additive measures.

drills.title: Model loan performance
drills.prompt: Design a model for monthly loan balances, payment events, and borrower attribute history.
drills.brief: Balances are periodic snapshots; payments are transactions.
drills.example: Mixing them creates duplicate balances when a loan has multiple payments.

rubric.label: Fact separation
rubric.description: Separates monthly snapshots from payment transactions.

rubric.label: Keys and dates
rubric.description: Names loan, borrower, snapshot month, and event dates.

rubric.label: Borrower history
rubric.description: Explains SCD treatment and point-in-time joins.

hints.conceptual: Separate state observed over time from events.
hints.pattern: Periodic snapshot fact + transaction fact + point-in-time dimension joins.

drills.solution: Create monthly loan snapshot and payment transaction facts, join conformed loan/date dimensions, and point-in-time join borrower SCD2 rows using effective dates.
drills.debrief: The two facts answer stock and flow questions without fan-out.

drills.title: Stop duplicate loads
drills.prompt: A retry doubled yesterday's orders. Diagnose the failure and design an idempotent repair with monitoring.
drills.brief: Reliable pipelines make retries safe and reconciliation visible.
drills.example: A stable source event key supports merge/upsert and duplicate checks.

rubric.label: Cause
rubric.description: Identifies append-on-retry or unstable keys/checkpoints.

rubric.label: Idempotent repair
rubric.description: Uses deterministic keys, merge/upsert, partition replacement, or transactional checkpoints.

rubric.label: Monitoring
rubric.description: Adds uniqueness, reconciliation, volume, and freshness checks.

hints.conceptual: Ask what identifies one source event across retries.
hints.pattern: Stable key → transactional merge/replace → source/target reconciliation.

drills.solution: Deduplicate by immutable source order ID, rebuild the affected partition, switch to transactional merge/checkpointing, and alert on key uniqueness, source-target counts, and freshness.
drills.debrief: Retries become ordinary when the same input always produces the same target state.

drills.title: Handle schema drift
drills.prompt: A vendor changes amount from numeric dollars to text cents and adds late records. Design detection, containment, and backfill.
drills.brief: Schema drift and lateness need explicit contracts, not silent coercion.
drills.example: Quarantine incompatible rows while preserving a replayable raw layer.

rubric.label: Detection
rubric.description: Uses schema contracts and distribution/unit checks.

rubric.label: Containment
rubric.description: Quarantines failures and preserves raw replay data.

rubric.label: Repair
rubric.description: Versions transformation, converts units, watermarks late data, and backfills idempotently.

hints.conceptual: Separate detecting bad contracts from replaying corrected transformations.
hints.pattern: Contract gate → quarantine/raw → versioned transform → watermark/backfill.

drills.solution: Fail the contract on type/unit drift, retain raw rows in quarantine, deploy a versioned cents-to-dollars transform, widen the event-time watermark, and replay affected partitions idempotently.
drills.debrief: Silent coercion would create plausible but wrong money values.

drills.title: Review an executive dashboard
drills.prompt: An executive dashboard has 24 equal-sized charts and no freshness label. Redesign it around a weekly revenue decision.
drills.brief: A dashboard is an interface for decisions, not a gallery of charts.
drills.example: Lead with outcome, drivers, exceptions, and data trust.

rubric.label: Decision
rubric.description: Names the audience, cadence, and decision.

rubric.label: Hierarchy
rubric.description: Prioritizes outcome, drivers, and exceptions.

rubric.label: Trust
rubric.description: Shows definitions, freshness, targets, and quality state.

hints.conceptual: Start with what someone must decide in the meeting.
hints.pattern: Outcome → drivers → exceptions → drill-down; always show freshness/definitions.

drills.solution: Lead with revenue versus plan, show a small driver tree and material exceptions, move diagnostics behind drill-downs, and display metric definitions, freshness, and data-quality state.
drills.debrief: Visual hierarchy encodes what deserves attention first.

drills.title: Design an operations control room
drills.prompt: Design a near-real-time dashboard for payment operations responding to incidents.
drills.brief: Operational dashboards optimize detection and action, not narrative reporting.
drills.example: Thresholds need owners and runbooks or they are decoration.

rubric.label: Signals
rubric.description: Uses rates, latency, errors, queues, and business impact.

rubric.label: Actionability
rubric.description: Includes thresholds, ownership, drill-downs, and runbooks.

rubric.label: Freshness
rubric.description: Shows event time, ingestion lag, and missing-data state.

hints.conceptual: Design for the first five minutes of an incident.
hints.pattern: Detect → scope → impact → owner/runbook, with lag and missing-data indicators.

drills.solution: Show success/error rates, latency and queue depth against thresholds, business impact and affected segments, event/ingestion lag, plus owned alerts and runbook drill-downs.
drills.debrief: The operator should move from symptom to bounded action without interpreting a wall of charts.

drills.title: Data Analyst: Growth review
drills.prompt: Plan a growth review that reconciles SQL results, segments a funnel change, and recommends one next action.
drills.brief: The analyst connects trustworthy computation to a decision.
drills.example: State the grain and denominator before explaining a trend.

rubric.label: Analysis
rubric.description: Covers grain, validation, segmentation, and action.

hints.conceptual: Connect data trust, diagnosis, and decision.
hints.pattern: Validate → query/segment → quantify → recommend.

drills.solution: Validate grain and tracking, query a reproducible funnel by segment, quantify the driver, then recommend a reversible next step.
drills.debrief: Strong analyst answers make the reasoning reproducible.

drills.title: Business Analyst: Process redesign
drills.prompt: Turn a vague request to improve onboarding into requirements, measures, risks, and acceptance criteria.
drills.brief: Business analysis makes ambiguity testable.
drills.example: Separate stakeholder outcomes from proposed solutions.

rubric.label: Requirements
rubric.description: Covers stakeholders, current state, metrics, constraints, and acceptance.

hints.conceptual: Make success and boundaries observable.
hints.pattern: Stakeholders → current/future state → rules → metrics → acceptance.

drills.solution: Map stakeholders and current state, define business rules and exceptions, measure cycle time/quality, and write testable acceptance criteria.
drills.debrief: The deliverable is shared decision clarity, not a long document.

drills.title: Product Analyst: Activation
drills.prompt: Define activation, diagnose a decline, and design a test for an onboarding change.
drills.brief: Product analysis joins measurement, diagnosis, and experimentation.
drills.example: An activation event should predict retained value, not just happen early.

rubric.label: Product reasoning
rubric.description: Defines activation, segments causes, and designs a guarded experiment.

hints.conceptual: Link early behavior to retained value.
hints.pattern: Define → validate prediction → diagnose → experiment.

drills.solution: Choose an early event predictive of retention, validate it by cohort, locate the decline by segment/step, then test a change with conversion and quality guardrails.
drills.debrief: Activation is a validated leading indicator, not a convenient click.

drills.title: Revenue Analyst: Forecast miss
drills.prompt: Explain a revenue forecast miss by price, volume, mix, retention, and timing, then propose controls.
drills.brief: Finance analysis reconciles definitions before explaining variance.
drills.example: Mix can move average price even when every segment price is unchanged.

rubric.label: Variance bridge
rubric.description: Reconciles actuals and separates price, volume, mix, retention, and timing.

hints.conceptual: Build an additive bridge from plan to actual.
hints.pattern: Reconcile → bridge drivers → identify controllable cause → update forecast/control.

drills.solution: Reconcile source totals, bridge plan to actual by price/volume/mix/churn/timing, isolate controllable drivers, and update assumptions with owner-based variance controls.
drills.debrief: A forecast explanation should tie exactly to the observed miss.

drills.title: Analytics Engineer: Trusted metric
drills.prompt: Design and ship a trusted net-revenue model with tests, documentation, lineage, and safe incremental processing.
drills.brief: Analytics engineering turns definitions into dependable shared data products.
drills.example: A model is not trusted until grain, ownership, tests, and recovery are explicit.

rubric.label: Data product
rubric.description: Covers grain, metric definition, incremental strategy, tests, lineage, docs, and ownership.

hints.conceptual: Treat the metric as an operated product.
hints.pattern: Contract/grain → model → incremental/recovery → tests → docs/lineage/owner.

drills.solution: Define net revenue and grain, build idempotent incremental facts with late-data replay, test keys/relationships/reconciliation, document semantics and lineage, and assign ownership/SLAs.
drills.debrief: Trust comes from reproducible semantics and operational controls together.
